28:1.sourceText: Ὀψὲ δὲ σαββάτων, τῇ ἐπιφωσκούσῃ εἰς μίαν σαββάτων, ἦλθεν Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία θεωρῆσαι τὸν τάφον.
28:1.targetText: Now after [the] Sabbaths, it being dawn, toward the first [day] of the weeks, Mary the Magdalene came, and the other Mary, to see the grave,

groups.note: The actual dative article/dawning participle supplies the temporal it being dawn expression; its source remains that verbal construction, without an independent Greek be verb or it pronoun.

The actual μίαν is the cardinal one in the calendar expression, rendered the first [day]. The temporal unit day is supplied in English; no separate Greek day noun or πρῶτος first ordinal is printed here.
The actual σαββάτων is the same Sabbath/week head used in the calendar expression, rendered weeks here. It is not relabeled as a separately printed ἑβδομάς week noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the bracketed article before Sabbaths; the actual Greek Sabbaths noun is anarthrous.

28:2.sourceText: καὶ ἰδοὺ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας· ἄγγελος γὰρ Κυρίου καταβὰς ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καὶ προσελθὼν ἀπεκύλισεν τὸν λίθον καὶ ἐκάθητο ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ.
28:2.targetText: and behold, there came a great earthquake, for a messenger of the LORD, having come down out of Heaven, having come, rolled away the stone from the door, and was sitting on it,

groups.note: The actual γίνομαι event verb supplies there came with earthquake; the original head remains γίνομαι rather than a printed ἔρχομαι coming verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek καί connecting descending and approaching is not separately expressed as an English conjunction between those two participles.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes a from-the-door phrase after the stone; pinned N1904 has rolled away the stone without that added door phrase.

28:3.sourceText: ἦν δὲ ἡ εἰδέα αὐτοῦ ὡς ἀστραπὴ, καὶ τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτοῦ λευκὸν ὡς χιών.
28:3.targetText: and his countenance was as lightning, and his clothing white as snow,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with his countenance or his clothing.

28:4.sourceText: ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ φόβου αὐτοῦ ἐσείσθησαν οἱ τηροῦντες καὶ ἐγενήθησαν ὡς νεκροί.
28:4.targetText: and from the fear of him the keepers shook, and they became as dead men.

groups.note: The actual present keeping participle is substantival, rendered keepers for the people watching. Its source remains the keeping verb rather than an independently printed guards noun.

28:5.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν ταῖς γυναιξίν Μὴ φοβεῖσθε ὑμεῖς· οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον ζητεῖτε·
28:5.targetText: And the messenger answering said to the women, “Do not fear, for I have known that you seek Jesus who has been crucified;

unmappedSource.reason: The actual emphatic personal ὑμεῖς after the fear command is not separately expressed as an English subject word; the English command retains its addressed plural subject implicitly.

28:6.sourceText: οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε· ἠγέρθη γὰρ καθὼς εἶπεν· δεῦτε ἴδετε τὸν τόπον ὅπου ἔκειτο.
28:6.targetText: He is not here, for He rose, as He said; come, see the place where the LORD was lying;

groups.note: The actual ἠγέρθη is aorist passive, rendered He rose; its source passive raising form remains rather than a substituted active rising verb.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly names the LORD as the lying subject; pinned N1904 has where was lying without a written LORD title here.

28:7.sourceText: καὶ ταχὺ πορευθεῖσαι εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὅτι Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἰδοὺ προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε. ἰδοὺ εἶπον ὑμῖν.
28:7.targetText: and having gone quickly, say to His disciples that He rose from the dead; and behold, He goes before you to Galilee, there you will see Him; behold, I have told you.”

groups.note: The actual εἶπον is aorist indicative, rendered I have told. The source remains aorist rather than a Greek perfect form.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before Galilee is not separately expressed in English.

28:8.sourceText: καὶ ἀπελθοῦσαι ταχὺ ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου μετὰ φόβου καὶ χαρᾶς μεγάλης ἔδραμον ἀπαγγεῖλαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ.
28:8.targetText: And having gone forth quickly from the tomb, with fear and great joy, they ran to tell His disciples;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with His disciples.

28:9.sourceText: καὶ ἰδοὺ Ἰησοῦς ὑπήντησεν αὐταῖς λέγων Χαίρετε. αἱ δὲ προσελθοῦσαι ἐκράτησαν αὐτοῦ τοὺς πόδας καὶ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ.
28:9.targetText: and as they were going to tell His disciples, then behold, Jesus met them, saying, “Greetings!” And having come near, they laid hold of His feet, and worshiped Him.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with His feet.

unmappedTarget.text: as they were going to tell His disciples, then
unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes a fuller introductory going/telling clause and then; pinned N1904 begins directly with and behold Jesus met them without that added clause.

28:10.sourceText: τότε λέγει αὐταῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Μὴ φοβεῖσθε· ὑπάγετε ἀπαγγείλατε τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς μου ἵνα ἀπέλθωσιν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, κἀκεῖ με ὄψονται.
28:10.targetText: Then Jesus says to them, “Do not fear, go away, tell My brothers that they may go away to Galilee, and there they will see Me.”

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with Jesus, My brothers or Galilee.

28:11.sourceText: Πορευομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἰδού τινες τῆς κουστωδίας ἐλθόντες εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀπήγγειλαν τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν ἅπαντα τὰ γενόμενα.
28:11.targetText: And while they are going on, behold, certain of the guard having come into the city, reported to the chief priests all the things that happened,

groups.note: The actual going participle supplies the while ... are going on genitive-absolute construction; no separately printed Greek while/be words are invented.

28:12.sourceText: καὶ συναχθέντες μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων συμβούλιόν τε λαβόντες ἀργύρια ἱκανὰ ἔδωκαν τοῖς στρατιώταις
28:12.targetText: and having been gathered together with the elders, having also taken counsel, they gave much money to the soldiers,

28:13.sourceText: λέγοντες Εἴπατε ὅτι Οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ νυκτὸς ἐλθόντες ἔκλεψαν αὐτὸν ἡμῶν κοιμωμένων.
28:13.targetText: saying, “Say that His disciples having come by night, stole Him—we being asleep;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with His disciples.

28:14.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν ἀκουσθῇ τοῦτο ἐπὶ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος, ἡμεῖς πείσομεν καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀμερίμνους ποιήσομεν.
28:14.targetText: and if this is heard by the governor, we will persuade him, and you keep free from anxiety.”

groups.note: The actual ἐπί/genitive governor phrase is rendered by the governor in the hearing clause; its source remains the original preposition/case constituent rather than a substituted ὑπό agent phrase.

The actual named governor is the hearing party in the condition and the same person to be persuaded in its immediate response. English repeats him under persuading; both mentions retain that one real governor identity, without a separately printed original object pronoun.
The actual ποιήσομεν is future making/causing, rendered keep with the anxiety-free state adjective. The source remains ποιέω rather than a separately printed τηρέω keeping verb.

28:15.sourceText: οἱ δὲ λαβόντες ἀργύρια ἐποίησαν ὡς ἐδιδάχθησαν. Καὶ διεφημίσθη ὁ λόγος οὗτος παρὰ Ἰουδαίοις μέχρι τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.
28:15.targetText: And they, having received the money, did as they were taught, and this account was spread abroad among Jews until this day.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with this account.
The Greek article is not separately expressed with the English this-day time designation.

28:16.sourceText: Οἱ δὲ ἕνδεκα μαθηταὶ ἐπορεύθησαν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, εἰς τὸ ὄρος οὗ ἐτάξατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς,
28:16.targetText: And the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus appointed them,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles before Galilee and Jesus are not separately expressed in English.

28:17.sourceText: καὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν προσεκύνησαν, οἱ δὲ ἐδίστασαν.
28:17.targetText: and having seen Him, they worshiped Him, but some wavered.

groups.note: The actual αὐτόν names the seen person and the same immediate worship object. English repeats Him with worshiping; both mentions retain the one actual written person pronoun.
The actual article-led contrasting group οἱ δέ is rendered but some. The source remains that substantive article construction, without an independently printed τινές some word.

28:18.sourceText: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς λέγων Ἐδόθη μοι πᾶσα ἐξουσία ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
28:18.targetText: And having come near, Jesus spoke to them, saying, “All authority in Heaven and on earth was given to Me;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles before Jesus and earth are not separately expressed in English.

28:19.sourceText: πορευθέντες οὖν μαθητεύσατε πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, βαπτίζοντες αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ Υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος,
28:19.targetText: having gone, then, disciple all the nations, immersing them into the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit,

28:20.sourceText: διδάσκοντες αὐτοὺς τηρεῖν πάντα ὅσα ἐνετειλάμην ὑμῖν· καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰμι πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας ἕως τῆς συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος.
28:20.targetText: teaching them to observe all, whatever I commanded you, and behold, I am with you all the days—until the full end of the age.”
